ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis is day length (hours), from 0 to 24; the vertical axis is noon solar altitude, from 0° to 90°. Number 5 is located at the far right end of the figure, and its horizontal coordinate corresponds to a day length of about 24 hours; its vertical coordinate is between 0° and 45°, about a noon solar altitude of 23.5°. Then reason: A day length of 24 hours indicates that the place is in polar day. Use the noon solar altitude formula H=90°-|latitude−latitude of the direct solar point|. If it is December 22, the sun is directly over the Tropic of Capricorn, and the latitude of the direct solar point δ≈23.5°S; the latitude of the South Pole is 90°S. Substituting gives H=90°-|90°S−23.5°S|=23.5°. At this time, the South Pole is in polar day, with a day length of 24 hours and a noon solar altitude of about 23.5°, which matches the position of 5 in the figure. Therefore, what 5 in the figure may represent is the South Pole on December 22.
